16d1caeac2a7d8ab2470d56fe8231aaec0251c5d.summary: Rapid7 Labs blog post (published 2013-08-19) by Claudio 'nex' Guarnieri describes ByeByeShell, a basic custom reverse-shell backdoor spread by spearphishing in a campaign mostly directed at Pakistani targets. Lures were Pakistan-politics documents that reused news articles, and no exploit was used. The report makes no attribution and says the origin of the attacks is unclear. The operators are assumed to have kept the campaign running for at least the last 6 months. The author emulated the backdoor's command server to observe operator behaviour.

countries.q: ByeBye Shell and the targeting of Pakistan

dates.what: Rapid7 Labs blog post analysing the ByeBye Shell campaign was published

tools.q: the malware creates and launches a Cabinet Self-Extractor, which drops two additional executable

techniques.q: social engineering the victim through well-crafted spearphishing emails.
custom reverse shell with just a handful of features.
Override Unicode character in order to twist the .exe file extension into something more credible.

hedges: The attackers probably just relied on social engineering rather than exploits; no exploit was used in the attacks attributed to this campaign.
The campaign appears to have been active since at least the beginning of the year.
The ByeByeShell name is the author's own label, given due to a lack of public literature about the case.
No clear indicator is available to make an informed estimate of the origin of the attacks.
The operators are assumed, not confirmed, to have kept operations running for at least the last 6 months, possibly even more.
